experiment: M1C.5 — boundary-gated rebound theory: analytic reduction of the churn switching gate (analysis/verification of existing canonical A trajectories, no new model)
research_question: Can the empirically observed boundary gate (M1C.4: a < 0.55 never rebounds, a >= 0.8 always rebounds) be derived analytically from the M1C.3 exact rebound criterion?

canonical_specialization.boundary_relation: D(a) = D_max and F(a) = a + D_max exactly (a = j*/K is the argmax of D)

theory_chain.region1_reduction: M*Delta(j) - gamma(j) = (1-alpha)D(j) - D_max + alpha*h(j/K) on the swept prefix, h(x) = x[F_a(2-x)-1], F_a = a + D_max
theory_chain.state_reduced_bound: residual <= alpha*(max_j h(j/K) - D_max) because (1-alpha)D(j) - D_max <= -alpha*D_max
theory_chain.maximization: F_a <= 1/2 -> h <= 0 -> rebound impossible (exact); F_a > 1/2 -> interior max at x* = 1 - 1/(2F_a) with value (2F_a-1)^2/(4F_a); x* <= a iff (a+D_max)(1-a) <= 1/2 which holds for all canonical A states (D_max <= 0.25 < sqrt(2)-1)
theory_chain.threshold: necessary gate: a > a_crit(D_max) with a_crit(D) = [(1-D) + sqrt(D(D+2))]/2 (large root; continuum-style envelope, discrete grid max differs by O(1/K^2) rounding)
theory_chain.logic_direction: a <= a_crit => rebound impossible (provable direction). a > a_crit is NECESSARY only, NOT sufficient: the residual additionally needs (1-alpha)D(j) close to its bound, i.e. D(j) near D_max at the gate-maximizing prefix

profile_factor.P(x_r): D(x_r)/D_max at the rebound-driving prefix x_r (realized argmax of the residual); compares rebound rounds vs gate-open contraction rounds
profile_factor.status: simple diagnostic, not a new formalism

churn_window: as M1C.4: first D_max < 0.05 (onset, M1B.2 divider) through t_stop - 1
no_post_hoc_tuning: a_crit closed form fixed by the M1C.3 criterion; no parameter adjusted to fit the observed 0.58 gate
